one_month_reasoning: Window 2026-10-06 to 2026-11-05. Scheduled event: Q3-26 results, expected late October (date not yet announced). They are likely to bring the first 2027 capex numbers ('increase significantly' per the CFO [10]) and the first 10-Q disclosure of ATM use. Recent earnings weeks moved the stock about +/-10%: the Q2 print fell ~4% after hours [10], then the week of Jul 27 closed at $356 vs $320 the prior week [43]. The Q3 GAAP line will also carry the SpaceX mark. SpaceX weekly closes ran $108-159 through Q3 versus $162 in the week of Jun 29 [43], so expect a small equity-security loss against Q2's $99B gain: a headline optics risk, but consensus ex-gains EPS is what moves the stock. Other in-window items: peers' capex guides (MSFT/META/AMZN late Oct) and the DOJ's appeal decision on the ad tech remedies. I have no edge on the direction of the print. Strong Cloud/backlog is likely, but a large 2027 capex step-up has been sold on the day twice this year. So I center slightly below spot (median ~$346) with sigma ~9.5% for the month (32%/3.5 = 9.1%, plus a little for earnings). P(>= spot) = 0.48.

fair_value.method: Blend of P/E (65%) and EV/EBITDA (35%) priced at the 2027-10-06 horizon on NTM estimates. P/E: 21.8x x haircut NTM EPS $16.08 x 0.995 + $10.75/share haircut equity stakes = $360. EV/EBITDA: 10.5x x NTM EBITDA $361.8B + $156.7B non-operating assets, / 12.35B shares = $320. Blend = $346.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM EPS at Oct-27 $16.08 (consensus 2027 $14.95, 2028 $17.89 cut 8%) x 21.8x x (1-0.5% dilution) + $10.75 equity stakes

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus has EBIT margin rising from 34.4% (2026) to 35.9% (2028) while consensus capex climbs $201.7B -> $301.0B -> $339.5B [15]; CFO said the infrastructure build 'will continue to put pressure on the P&L in the form of higher depreciation' and flagged near-term margin pressure from third-party capacity [10]. Q2 FCF was already -$5.9B [1]. Haircut = holding 2028 EBIT margin roughly flat at ~33% instead of 35.9% (about -8% on EPS). [citation gate 2026-10-06: CFO quotes verified in Alphabet's own Q2 transcript PDF (s206.q4cdn.com ... 2026_Q2_Earnings_Transcript.pdf); consensus EBIT and capex verified at MarketScreener]

Calendarized CY2027 P/E of 10 peers: median 19.8x (range 13.2x-33.7x); ex-China (7 US names) median 23.5x. 21.8x sits between the two (equal to META, the closest ad-funded AI-capex peer) and below GOOGL's current 23.2x CY27 P/E [14].

Preferred converts into ~43-54M shares (19M preferred x 2.252-2.842) [4]; part of the $40B ATM [5] could add up to ~115M shares at ~$350. Assume ~60M net of what consensus share counts already include: ~0.5% of 12.23B.

SpaceX shares $94.1B (80.0 short-term + 14.1 long-term restricted) x 75% + non-marketable equity $124.3B x 50% = $70.6B + $62.2B = $132.8B / 12.35B shares. Haircuts are judgment: lock-ups, concentration, marks set at peak AI valuations.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: 10.5x x NTM EBITDA $361.8B = $3,799B EV + net cash $24.0B + equity stakes $132.8B = $3,956B / 12.35B shares

inputs_detail.derivation: Peer CY2027 EV/EBITDA median 10.2x (range 6.5x-25.7x); US-only median 10.8x. 10.5x is between. No premium for GOOGL's 13.9x because EBITDA excludes the depreciation of a $200-300B/yr capex program, so EBITDA overstates owner earnings more for GOOGL than for asset-light peers. [citation gate 2026-10-06: the 10.2x / 10.8x medians use MarketScreener EVs (aggregator). From filings (EV = Oct 6 close x cover shares + debt - cash and current marketable securities, latest 10-Q/10-K XBRL; over calendarized MarketScreener CY2027 EBITDA) the US-7 median is 10.5x: MSFT 14.6, AMZN 10.2, META 10.5, AAPL 26.5, ORCL 8.1, NFLX 14.6, CRM 10.5. China anchors (TCEHY, BABA, BIDU) could not be verified from filings]

inputs_detail.input: Net cash (ex SpaceX) projected to Oct-2027
inputs_detail.derivation: 6/30/26 cash+short-term investments $242.5B less $80.0B SpaceX held in marketable securities less debt $100.2B = $62.3B; + H2-26 FCF $4.2B (2026 consensus FCF $8.4B less H1 FCF $4.3B = OCF $84.9B - capex $80.6B) + 0.75 x 2027 consensus FCF (-$36.7B) - 5 quarters common dividends ($0.22 x 12.23B) - preferred dividends (6.25% x $19.0B x 1.25 years).
12.230B shares outstanding at 6/30/26 + ~45-55M from the mandatory convertible + ~70M from SBC/ATM drift (no buybacks in H1-26).

bear.story: AI-capex payback doubts deepen: the 2027 capex guide (consensus ~$301B) lands with Cloud growth slowing as third-party bridging capacity and depreciation squeeze margins. Anthropic-concentrated backlog [31] and circular financing [32] become the story. The ATM is drawn, search share keeps slipping (StatCounter 89.9% in Sep-26 [35]) and the DOJ cross-appeal keeps a structural search remedy alive. NTM EPS ~10% below my already-haircut $16.08 (~$14.5) at 17x (ORCL/NFLX level) + $10.75 stakes = ~$257. [citation gate 2026-10-06: [31]/[32] are press-only; context, not used in any supervisor number]

base.story: Search grows low-teens and Cloud converts backlog, but depreciation caps margin expansion and FCF stays near zero through 2027. Equity issuance replaces buybacks. Multiple drifts from 23x to ~22x NTM: roughly flat over 12 months, in line with fair value ~$346.

bull.story: Consensus proves right or low: 2028 EPS ~$17.9, TPU external sales ramp in 2027 [10], Cloud margin keeps expanding (Q2 OI $8.8B on $24.8B revenue [1]), ATM left unused. 25x NTM consensus EPS $17.16 + $10.75 stakes = ~$440, near the $429 average analyst target [16].

comps_summary.peer_range: Basis: calendar-2027 consensus from MarketScreener, with non-December fiscal years calendarized by month-weighting the two overlapping fiscal-year multiples (earnings-weighted harmonic). P/E 13.2x (BIDU) to 33.7x (AAPL), median 19.8x (US-only median 23.5x). EV/EBITDA 6.5x to 25.7x, median 10.15x (US-only median 10.8x).
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: P/E 21.8x: above the 10-peer median (19.8x), below the US-only median (23.5x) and below GOOGL's own 23.2x CY27. EV/EBITDA 10.5x: at the peer medians, well below GOOGL's 13.9x.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: P/E: the small premium to the all-peer median reflects only the structural China-ADR discount that pulls the median down (TCEHY/BABA/BIDU at 13-15x). GOOGL's consensus CY27 EPS growth (~+26% vs an underlying 2026 of $11.89) is well above the peer median (~+10%), which would argue for a premium. I do not give one because (a) consensus 2027 FCF is negative (-$36.7B) [15] while capex rises to ~$301B, (b) the company has moved from buying back ~$13B a quarter to issuing equity (~$30.5B of common in H1-26, $19B of mandatory convertible preferred, a $40B ATM) [1][4][5], and (c) over 40% of the Cloud backlog reportedly sits with one customer, Anthropic, which Google also funds [31][32]. None of this shows that above-peer growth will persist on a per-share, cash basis through Oct-2027. EV/EBITDA: no premium, because EBITDA leaves out the depreciation of the capex program. [citation gate 2026-10-06: 'over 40% of the Cloud backlog with Anthropic' and the Google financing backstop are press reports (The Information via Silicon UK), not in Alphabet's 10-Q: context only, not used in any supervisor number]

thesis_break_reason: $255 is the bear-case value: ~17x a 10%-lower NTM EPS plus haircut stakes, and below the Mar-2026 trough ($274.34 weekly close [43]). Trading there would mean the market has stopped capitalizing the AI build-out at peer multiples. Likely causes: a 2027 capex guide with no matching Cloud/TPU revenue, an Anthropic-concentrated backlog wobble, a visible step-down in Search growth, or heavy ATM use. That is a fundamental re-rating, not ordinary 32%-vol noise around fair value $346.

key_uncertainties: Whether 2027 capex (consensus ~$301B, after ~$200B in 2026) earns a return before depreciation catches up. Consensus 2027 FCF is -$36.7B.
Backlog quality: over 40% of the $514B Cloud backlog reportedly sits with Anthropic, which Google also funds (up to $40B) and whose TPU purchases Google helps finance.
Per-share dilution path: $40B ATM, mandatory convertible preferred (converts May-2029), no buybacks since Q1-26.
GAAP earnings quality: equity-security gains were $135.9B of $216.2B H1-26 pretax income (63%), so headline EPS and P/E (17.4x trailing) look cheaper than the operating business is.
Search share erosion to chat assistants (StatCounter <90% in Sep-26) versus record Search usage claimed by management.
Search-case cross-appeal (DOJ seeking stronger remedies) and the EU DMA decision.
Credit-market tolerance: new-issue spreads widened 16-35bp between the Feb-26 and Aug-26 deals despite AA+/Aa2 ratings.
reasoning: Skeptic lane. Starting facts (filings): Q2-26 revenue $119.8B (+24%), operating income $40.8B, Cloud $24.8B (+82%) with $8.8B OI, Cloud backlog $513.9B [1][2]. What the consensus may be underweighting: (1) Earnings quality. H1-26 pretax income $216.2B includes $135.9B of equity-security gains (SpaceX IPO and other marks; $94.1B of SpaceX stock, mostly locked up [2][42]) [9][1], so trailing P/E of ~17x is misleading. On ex-gains consensus the stock is 23.2x CY27 [14]. (2) Cash. Q2 FCF -$5.9B, TTM $53.3B [1]. Consensus FCF is $8.4B in 2026 and -$36.7B in 2027 on capex of $201.7B and $301.0B [15], consistent with the standing AI-capex view (Alphabet 2027 consensus $285-357B) [40]. Purchase commitments jumped to $707B [3]. (3) Funding mix. Buybacks went from $13.2B in Q2-25 to zero [1]. Alphabet sold 58M Class A/C shares (net $20.5B) plus $10B to Berkshire, $19B of 6.25% mandatory convertibles, and set up a $40B ATM [4][5][6], plus $45B of bonds in Feb/Aug [7][8][39]. (4) Credit is pricing more risk. On like-for-like tenors, new-issue spreads widened from Feb to Aug: 10y T+63 -> T+85, 40y T+95 -> T+130, despite unchanged AA+/Aa2 ratings [7][8]. The Feb sterling deal included a 2126 century bond at gilts +120bp [41]. That is a mild, not alarming, signal. (5) Concentration and circularity. Anthropic reportedly accounts for over 40% of the backlog [31], and Google backstops financing of Anthropic's TPU purchases [32]. These are press reports (The Information, via Silicon UK), used here only to size bear-case probability, not as valuation inputs. (6) Sentiment is crowded: 0 sells and 4 holds out of 55 analysts; insiders sold ~$8.7M and bought $0 over 3 months [37]. Visible Form 4s are routine 10b5-1 or vesting [11][12][13], so this is not a red flag. Alt-data and markets: StatCounter puts Google at 89.94% of worldwide search in Sep-26 [35]. On Kalshi (via Octagon, Oct 2, week of Oct 5), 'Above 20.5%' Google share of OpenRouter text-model requests traded ~75% and 'Above 19.9%' 97%, with 30,430 contracts on the latter [36]. That reads as a solid but not dominant AI-model position. Privacy litigation remains a recurring cost (shareholder proponents cite a $425.7M privacy jury verdict [38]; PriceRunner $2.1B damages and the $5.2B EU Android payment in Q2-Q3 [3]). What weakens the bear case: the ad tech remedy decision rejected the AdX divestiture and imposed a 6-year behavioral decree [27][28][29][30], removing the largest structural legal tail. The balance sheet remains AA+. Operating momentum is real. Valuation: P/E (21.8x, between the all-peer median 19.8x and the US median 23.5x) on haircut NTM EPS gives $360. EV/EBITDA at the peer median (10.5x) gives $320. Blended fair value is $346, about 0.5% below spot. Scenarios: 257/348/440 at 25/50/25 (mean ~$348). The ladder is a lognormal mixture around those (sigma 0.22/0.17/0.17), giving a log-sd of ~0.27 and median ~$348. This is somewhat tighter than the 32% realized vol, because the realized figure includes the Mar-May 2026 re-rating (weekly close $274 in late March to a $408.61 high in May) [43], and wider than base-rate large-cap moves only in the left tail. Research limits: Twelve Data and Alpha Vantage estimate and statistics endpoints were plan-restricted, so consensus comes from MarketScreener and StockAnalysis. Seeking Alpha, Axios and some trade press were not fetchable.
